articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Actor Liam McIntyre Isn't Fazed by Players' Brutal Comments About the Game
articles.summary: Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose. Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild for many players worldwide, and opinions have been strong, to say the least.
body: One of the core topics of the Wolverine debate is actor Liam McIntyre, who plays the game’s titular character. Some fans don’t believe he bears a close enough resemblance to the iconic mutant, while others feel that Insomniac’s face scans and art style didn’t do his visage justice.

McIntyre has been excitedly posting about his role as Wolverine ever since his involvement was first announced, and some players have just now realized that he’s been seeing what they’re saying about him on social media this entire time.
In response to one of these players, McIntyre lightheartedly remarked that he’s seen much worse said about him ever since he started his acting career.

“Ha. Man, my career started with the responsibility of taking over for the incredible Andy Whitfield in Spartacus (RIP to that legend). I've read things you couldn't believe:) I just hope everyone has fun. I'm proud as hell of this game. It's a blast,” he wrote on X.
points: Wolverine actor Liam McIntyre has seen what fans are saying about him and Insomniac's latest superhero game, but it's no skin off his nose.
Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild for many players worldwide, and opinions have been strong, to say the least.

articles.title: 10 Near-Perfect Xbox 360 Games Nobody Played
articles.summary: The Xbox brand kicked off in 2001 with an enormous black box that proved Microsoft could hang with the major console players just fine. However, the Xbox 360 was the hardware that revealed Xbox had the potential to dominate the space, thanks in part to hits like Halo 2 and Gears of War.
body: Many of the games from the Xbox 360 era are rightly remembered as classics. But there are other amazing titles — the platform’s true hidden gems — that deserved much more attention and acclaim than they ever received. Here are 10 near-perfect Xbox 360 games nobody played.

There was actually some drama around Ridge Racer 6, one of Xbox 360’s first games. It was a solid racing game, but also the next entry in a popular PlayStation franchise, and released exclusively on Microsoft’s new console. Unfortunately for Namco, it faced a lot of competition from other titles in the launch lineup, including the excellent Project Gotham Racing 3 from Microsoft, as well as Need for Speed: Most Wanted from Electronic Arts. Those other games overshadowed Namco’s potential hit, at least in North America.

However, the Xbox 360 was the hardware that revealed Xbox had the potential to dominate the space, thanks in part to hits like Halo 2 and Gears of War.

articles.title: Wardogs Players Are Avoiding One of the Game's Factions Because It Has a Stigma of Attracting the Stupidest Players
articles.summary: Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games. There are three playable teams in Wardogs: a blue team (Lonestar), a red team (Valkyra), and a green team (Manticore).
body: Other teams also fill up extremely quickly because of the stigma, meaning more inexperienced players who don't know any better are sometimes shut out of having other options. One player on Reddit noted that some matches have delayed starts, simply because some players refuse to pick Lonestar, and it leads to the game not starting the match due to a lack of players. You can see one viral clip of Lonestar's antics below to get an idea of the absurdity that some players are experiencing.

There are instances of Lonestar overcoming the odds and proving the doubters wrong. In my experience, I have never won on Lonestar. All of my wins in Wardogs come from playing with the other two teams. Is that a coincidence? It seems statistically unlikely, but maybe! Hopefully this will iron out as the game's player base becomes more experienced and more well-rounded, but who's to say when that will happen.
points: Wardogs players are avoiding the game's Lonestar faction, as they seemingly attract the worst players and lose the most games.

articles.title: EU Kids Act Could Require Gamers to Prove Their Age Before Playing Certain Games
articles.summary: The EU Kids Act will be presented before the European Parliament on Thursday, and if passed, will have a meaningful impact on gamers of all ages if they want access to certain kinds of games. The EU Kids Act is proposed legislation meant to keep children from being harmed online.
body: Documents obtained by Euractiv reportedly state that the act “will oblige providers of social media services and video-sharing platforms to perform age verification when a user opens a new account.”

The outlet added that, according to this document, these age verification requirements will extend to other services like AI chat bots and even “online games that are risky to minors.” It is not expected to impact industrial AI, AI office products, or educational online services.

This is the latest big age verification news to arise after PlayStation started rolling out age verification checks back in April across Ireland and the UK in order for players to access certain network features like voice chatting, messaging, and streaming. Users can verify their age via facial scan, mobile number, or their ID, though these methods can vary depending upon users’ specific "country or region."

And earlier this month, Australia implemented proof-of-age verification on Steam in order for players to access games rated R18+ — but unlike PlayStation, it will only accept Australian credit cards, which could lead to some difficulties for adult players in the region who don’t have one.
points: The EU Kids Act will be presented before the European Parliament on Thursday, and if passed, will have a meaningful impact on gamers of all ages if they want access to certain kinds of games.

articles.title: Blizzard Explains How Diablo 5 Avoids Diablo 4's Open-World Problem
articles.summary: If you watched the Diablo 5 panel at BlizzCon 2026, you likely heard that Blizzard is once again embracing procedural generation for the overworld in its forthcoming action RPG. This is a stark contrast to Diablo 4, which controversially had a mostly static open world for players to explore.
body: During a group Q&A that Polygon attended at BlizzCon, Diablo 5's game director and executive producer delved into how the team is embracing overworld procedural generation once again and learning from Diablo 4's biggest mistake. Hardcore Diablo fans will be happy to know the game will feature an overlay from day one, too.

Diablo 2 and 3 procedurally generated its outdoor open worlds, which connected dungeons, but Blizzard made the controversial decision to give Diablo 4 a static open world. While this was better tailored for Diablo 4' s online-focused approach, the community didn't love it. Now, even franchise executive producer Matt Zitterman admits that it was a real pitfall of Diablo 4, as it only allowed players to have a sense of discovery for a single time when they discovered a new area.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: Blizzard Says Diablo 5 Was Too Big To Be A Diablo 4 Expansion
articles.summary: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward. Instead, Blizzard is preparing to tell the darkest story yet in Diablo 5, one that required a new numbered game to properly reintroduce Diablo himself back to the series, following his defeat in 2012's Diablo…
body: Speaking to GameSpot at BlizzCon, Diablo senior production director Tiffany Wat and executive producer Matt Zitterman explained that it made sense for Blizzard to move to a new Diablo so that the studio could make structural changes to the game--changes that would have been very challenging to pull off within the framework of a Diablo 4 expansion.

"It really started by looking at who our players are," Zitterman said. "Who are Diablo players? Why are they playing Diablo? What do they want out of a Diablo game? That is a really critical step in the early conceptual phase for a game, even before you're thinking about, like, 'Gosh, should we make this an expansion? Should we make it a sequel? How do we do this?' Looking at past examples, looking at what's working well in Diablo 4, where there are opportunities for improvement, and we kind of build our ambition for the game at the conceptual phase through those avenues of information."
points: Diablo 4 is far from dead, but don't expect any new expansions for the game going forward.

articles.title: Wardogs Devs Are Watching Economy Cheaters Like Hawks
articles.summary: With the FPS Wardogs dominating the Steam charts, developer Bulkhead is paying close attention to the game's various systems. The studio recently dropped a new patch that makes some necessary changes for server stability, while confirming that the team has their eyes on cheaters and exploiters.
body: As part of Patch 0.11, which came out on September 14, Bulkhead announced that should any dogs of war take advantage of Wardogs' economy by farming servers, they'll find themselves either temporarily or permanently banned from the game.
"As an early access game, we’re not perfect, and we never will be," Bulkhead said in the patch notes. "But if you do find something and take advantage of it, we have decided to come down hard."
To be specific, Bulkhead outlined three different scenarios that will come with three different repercussions depending on the type of exploit you partake in.

Scenario 1: Stockpiling money by abusing cash exploits and bugs will result in a timed ban, with the length determined by whether you were banned previously. Your cash and experience will get reset, too.

articles.title: New Steam Game Is Like Balatro Meets Newgrounds-Era Flash Games
articles.summary: It’s not often that I feel like I need to begin a video game recommendation with a health warning, but Kaz earns one. The ultra-fast indie game I’m about to tell you about can wreak havoc on your wrists if you play it for too long at once. Trust me, I know.
body: Developed by Kalinarm, Kaz is a new roguelike that’s available on Steam for $7. Its price tag matches its small scope; the elegant arcade game doubles down on a straightforward premise that you’ll feel compelled to dive into over and over again. Just make sure you have a strong keyboard and an ice pack handy.

Easy enough, right? Well, it would be if you didn’t have only 15 seconds to hit the level’s score threshold. Kaz is a lightning-fast game of reflexes. You need to work on instinct and muscle memory to meet the goal before the timer runs out, dodging traps and remembering to take down shielded enemies with two hits. It sounds simple, but that’s what makes Kaz such a great “one more level” game. I couldn’t stop loading up another run even when my wrists were starting to get sore because it was just so satisfying to test my typing speed.
points: It’s not often that I feel like I need to begin a video game recommendation with a health warning, but Kaz earns one.

articles.title: How WoW Forever Handles Its Massive Set Of New Quests
articles.summary: One of the big announcements at BlizzCon was WoW Forever, the next iteration of offering a classic-style WoW experience. Blizzard is hoping to draw players back to the OG WoW in a number of ways, including with the introduction of 1,000+ new quests.
body: If Blizzard is adding 1,000 more quests to WoW with the update, how many does that bring the game up to in total? It's a tricky question to answer, Greenfield said, in part because some of WoW's original quests are "tracking quests," but if you're counting "actual playable quests," the game has around 3,000 to 3,500.

So with 1,000+ more added of actual playable quests, that's a significant increase. WoW Forever also adds four new zones, and each of these has between 50 and 200 quests, so that's where many will come from. Additionally, the existing zones have been "glowed up," with the Wetlands and Azshara, specifically, getting a "lot of new quests to round them out as zones."
"Every nook and cranny, you're going to find something, even from like level five... onward, you're going to start seeing new stuff," Greenfield said.

Also in our interview, we asked how Blizzard came up with the inspirations for the 1,000 new quests, and if there might be a new version of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, which is regarded as perhaps the game's worst quest.
points: Blizzard is hoping to draw players back to the OG WoW in a number of ways, including with the introduction of 1,000+ new quests.

articles.title: Crazy Taxi Gets Crazier With Crazy Ex-Girlfriend Writers For New Movie
articles.summary: The Crazy Taxi franchise isn't just getting a brand-new game next year; it's also getting a live-action movie. Netflix and Sega have announced a new partnership that will see a Crazy Taxi film coming to the streaming service in 2027.
body: There's no director attached to the project, yet. However, Original Film's Neal H. Moritz and Toby Ascher are producing the Crazy Taxi movie, alongside Sonic the Hedgehog series producer Toru Nakahara. "This film is for anyone who's spent hours behind the wheel of a yellow cab on their Dreamcast, with the music cranked up, smashing through everything in sight just to make the next fare," said Moritz and Ascher in the Netflix press release.

The Netflix and Sega collaboration also includes a new Sonic animated show aimed at "an upper preschool audience," as well as a live-action movie based on Stranger Than Heaven. The latter is the newest game from developer RGG Studio--known for the Yakuza and Like A Dragon titles.

Meanwhile, it will be intriguing to see how much the Crazy Taxi movie ties into Crazy Taxi: World Tour. The new arcade racing game will feature lore this time, such as driver backstories for why they got behind the wheel in the first place.

Fascinatingly enough, Sega has been trying to get a Crazy Taxi movie out on the road for basically two decades. In fact, Superman and The Goonies director Richard Donner was attached to direct the adaptation at one point.
points: The Crazy Taxi franchise isn't just getting a brand-new game next year; it's also getting a live-action movie.

articles.title: The 10 Best Marvel Video Games Of All Time
articles.summary: Marvel heroes have been mainstays in video games since 1982, when Spider-Man first swung onto the Atari 2600 in a titular outing. But not every attempt to bring the dynamic heroes to digital life has met with success (if you don’t remember The Uncanny X-Men on the NES, your life is better for it).
body: At the movies, Marvel remains a hot property, as we learned from the success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day and the buzz around Avengers: Doomsday. But all of that stuff is for the future. In the present, we don’t have to wait to control our favorite heroes and villains because we already have a bunch of terrific options across a range of genres. Here are the 10 best Marvel video games of all time, available to play right now.

Developed by Firaxis Games, which is well-known for its work on the tactical XCOM series, Marvel’s Midnight Suns incorporates deck-building to let players use their army of heroes to thwart the resurrected Lilith. Turn-based combat incorporates environmental hazards, along with waves of enemies and chained attacks. There are 13 playable characters in the base game. Expansions have added another 4. It’s a surprisingly diverse group comprising heroes who are poised to factor heavily in future Marvel events. Ghost Rider is getting a new movie starring Ryan Gosling, for example.

articles.title: GTA 6's first confirmed actor is King of the Hill's Stephen Root: "It's an amazing thing to look at"
articles.summary: Rockstar Games hasn't said much about who's voicing the GTA 6 cast, but we now know at least one big-name actor attached to the upcoming crime epic: Stephen Root.
body: Internet sleuths have been scouring the web ever since the game's very first trailer, searching for even a whiff of the possible GTA 6 cast, and a recurring fan theory is now seemingly confirmed. Asked about the fan speculation by AP News, Stephen Root said, "Yeah, you're gonna see me in that."

You might recognise Root's face from his work in the Oscar-winning horror film Get Out and the Emmy-winning HBO series Barry, but his voice acting career is just as prolific. He has credits in everything from King of the Hill to Rick and Morty, and he even reprised his role as a bubble-loving yellow fish in the Finding Nemo video game.

"It's coming out November 19th, is the latest I know of," said Root. "But, I think, from the first roll out of GTA that they were doing maybe almost a year ago, they had my character in there and there were too many people who knew me from King of the Hill and my voice. So, I think that secret got divulged then."
points: Rockstar Games hasn't said much about who's voicing the GTA 6 cast, but we now know at least one big-name actor attached to the upcoming crime epic: Stephen Root.

articles.title: Marathon's permanent PvE mode and next major update delayed to December days before launch, and Bungie's "moving away from a strict season schedule"
articles.summary: Marathon Season 3 and everything that was due to come alongside it has been delayed, including the sci-fi shooter's long-awaited full PvE mode. Bungie's next major update is now launching in December instead, and the famed studio is pivoting away from seasonal updates entirely.
body: "We previously shared plans for Marathon's next major update to launch on September 22. We know many players were looking forward to it, and we appreciate your patience. We are adjusting our plans to ensure the update meets your expectations," Bungie wrote in a recent blog post. "The content originally planned for September will now arrive as part of our Symbiosis update on December 8."

December's Symbiosis update is promising a new Runner shell, the aforementioned permanent PvE mode, a social space where players can try out weapons together, improvements to the onboarding experience for newcomers, a "refreshed Perimeter zone" and an "experimental" team deathmatch mode.

Rather than a big seasonal feast next week, Marathon players can expect a slightly smaller update on 6 October that'll reset the game's progression and economy, while adding a new Rewards Pass and quality-of-life improvements. Vault Breaker, a different PvE mode that temporarily popped up a few months ago, will also return for a limited time.
points: Marathon Season 3 and everything that was due to come alongside it has been delayed, including the sci-fi shooter's long-awaited full PvE mode.

articles.title: Arc Raiders Expeditions may not come back: 'Maybe we'll scrap the whole system'
articles.summary: Embark Studios announced a "pause" on Expeditions in Arc Raiders until early 2027 so it can rework the system to address longstanding issues and complaints that can't be handled with "incremental fixes." In a recent interview with PCGamesN, though, Arc Raiders executive producer Aleksander Grøndal…
body: Expeditions are essentially Arc's equivalent of prestiging in Call of Duty: High-level players invest time and resources into a "caravan" that ultimately—within the context of the game's fiction—enables their character to leave the Rust Belt forever. Practically speaking, it's a full reset of levels, skills, and inventory, in exchange for certain unique benefits conferred upon the player's new character. It's a major undertaking, and many Arc players haven't been happy with the amount of grind involved for a relatively minor payoff.

Announcing the pause in August, Embark said many of the issues raised by players, "like the tight departure windows, the reward structure, and accessibility for new players, need more than incremental fixes. They call for bigger changes." The fifth Expedition, set to depart at the end of September, will be the last until Embark has the overhaul finished—or just cans the whole thing, as the case may be.

"Was the system perfect? No, probably not," Grøndal told PCGN at Gamescom. "We want to make some significant changes to the Expedition system. But I think right now we're focused on, 'Yeah, they are what they are,' but the intent is to have them change.

videos.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave — Overview Trailer — Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: The Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave game launches September 17, 2026, only on Nintendo Switch 2. Pre-orders are available now on Nintendo eShop:
body: Travel through time to gather allies and defeat the demon god Balor. Test your tactical prowess in battle as you guide four heroes on their interwoven journeys from past to present. Together, you’ll save the future from ruin—or fall trying.
Visit Nintendo.com for more info:

videos.title: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE – Demo Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Play the free demo for FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, available now on Nintendo Switch 2:
body: Return to the pixel-art world of FINAL FANTASY in this reimagined adventure! The world is full of secrets, including the wandering swordmaster Gilgamesh, a Colosseum with deadly monsters and rewards to match, the Chamber of Arms with formidable foes sealed within legendary weapons, and a showdown with Ultima Weapon. Pre-order the full game today or try out the first chapter with the free demo!
Visit Nintendo.com for more info:
